title: Venetian Carnival Wildlife Explorer
description: An interactive educational exhibit where students explore the cultural history of Venetian carnival masks alongside tropical parrot biodiversity. Users rotate and inspect both artifacts, answer quiz questions linking art history to natural science, and unlock animated sequences by correctly identifying facts about each subject.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive educational 3D explorer. Load venice_mask.glb on the left side and Parrot.glb on the right side of the scene, both on subtle circular pedestals (flat cylinders with metallic material). Use GLTFLoader to load both models. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 1.5, 5) looking at the origin. Add ambient light intensity 0.6, a directional light from (3, 5, 4) with intensity 1.2, and a soft hemisphere light. The background should be a gradient-like dark navy color (0x1a1a2e). Both models should slowly auto-rotate on their Y-axis. Implement OrbitControls with damping enabled but constrain vertical rotation between 10 and 80 degrees. Create an HTML overlay quiz panel at the bottom center of the screen. Implement a 6-step interactive quiz flow: Step 1: User clicks on the mask to highlight it (add emissive glow outline via a slightly scaled clone with backside rendering and emissive material), displaying info text about Venetian carnival masks. Step 2: User clicks the parrot to highlight it similarly, showing a fact about parrot species. Step 3: A multiple-choice question appears asking which century Venetian carnival masks became widespread (correct: 13th century). Validate the answer and show green/red feedback. Step 4: A question about parrot mimicry abilities appears. Validate answer. Step 5: User must drag a slider (HTML range input) to scale the parrot model between 0.5x and 2.0x to match a target size displayed as a translucent wireframe sphere, requiring precision within 5% tolerance. Validate the parameter. Step 6: User clicks a 'Complete Exhibit' button which triggers both models to play any embedded animations (use AnimationMixer), or if none exist, smoothly animate them moving toward center, spinning, and returning. Display a completion badge overlay with score out of 6. Use raycasting for object selection. Track and display the current step number and score throughout. All UI elements should use clean sans-serif fonts with semi-transparent dark backgrounds and rounded corners.
